author: Chris Richardson
title: Microservices.io
description: Java Champion and author of Microservices Patterns and POJOs in Action. Founded the original CloudFoundry.com, a Java platform that SpringSource bought in 2008, and later Eventuate, a framework for event-driven microservices. Consults and teaches on microservice architecture. Recent posts are an "Architecting for uncertainty" series that ties fast flow and Team Topologies to GenAI coding agents.

author: Mark Richards
title: Software Developer To Software Architect
description: Independent, hands-on software architect with more than 30 years' experience. Co-wrote Fundamentals of Software Architecture (2nd edition 2025) and Software Architecture: The Hard Parts with Neal Ford, and also Head First Software Architecture. The site is a series of short video lessons, now about one a month; recent ones cover transactional sagas, legacy migration and "architecture narratives".

author: Markus Winand
title: SQL Indexing and Tuning
description: Vienna-based SQL trainer and consultant, author of SQL Performance Explained. Also runs modern-sql.com, which tracks which databases support which SQL-standard features. Known for explaining indexing in a way that applies to any database. Posts very rarely; the latest is from December 2024.

author: Steve Smith
title: Ardalis
description: Founder of NimblePros, long-time Microsoft MVP and Pluralsight author. Maintains the Ardalis Clean Architecture template, GuardClauses, Specification and Result, and the DevIQ site. Recent posts cover running Claude Code agent teams on Windows and .NET memory use in Kubernetes, plus the occasional non-technical opinion piece.

author: Scott Hanselman
description: VP and Member of Technical Staff at Microsoft and GitHub, blogging for more than 20 years. Hosts Hanselminutes and Azure Friday, co-hosts Scott and Mark Learn To with Mark Russinovich, and helped open-source MS-DOS 4. Now posts only a few times a year, about home networking, Windows tooling and whether AI is killing the craft.

author: Andrew Lock
title: .NET Escapades
description: Works on Datadog's .NET SDK, Microsoft MVP and author of ASP.NET Core in Action. Maintains the NetEscapades libraries (EnumGenerators, SecurityHeaders). Posts every week in great detail; currently an "Exploring the .NET 11 preview" series, plus NativeAOT and web security.

author: Dave Callan
description: Irish .NET developer and Microsoft MVP, best known for daily .NET tips on LinkedIn. The blog has short how-tos on EF Core, caching, Visual Studio and dev tunnels, with only one post since February 2025.

author: Stephen Cleary
description: Go-to authority on async/await in .NET. Author of Concurrency in C# Cookbook and the Nito.AsyncEx library, Microsoft MVP and a prolific Stack Overflow answerer. Posts rarely (last in December 2024), usually long series such as the one on cancellation.

author: Jon Skeet
description: Top-ranked Stack Overflow user and author of C# in Depth and the Noda Time library. Spent many years at Google on the .NET client libraries for Google Cloud, and wrote in July 2026 of being "between jobs". Recent posts are about C# records and immutable collections, a hobby UK election-results site (Election 2029) and forking the managed-midi library.

author: Jimmy Bogard
description: Creator of AutoMapper and MediatR, advocate of Vertical Slice Architecture, and long-time consultant (formerly chief architect at Headspring). Both libraries became commercial in 2025 under Lucky Penny Software. Posts are now mostly release and licensing notes plus Vertical Slice Architecture training.

author: Chris Patterson
title: PhatBoyG.com
description: Creator of MassTransit, the .NET message-bus library; version 9 is now sold commercially by a company called Massient. The blog hasn't been updated since 2020 (the videos moved to YouTube).

author: Mattias Karlsson
title: devlead
description: Partner and technical fellow at WCOM AB in Gothenburg. A maintainer of Cake (the C# build tool) and LitJSON, and of about 30 other .NET packages, which together have a quarter of a billion NuGet downloads. Writes about .NET tooling: Cake.Sdk, file-based C# apps, Renovate and SLNX.

author: Steven Giesel
description: Switzerland-based .NET developer and Microsoft MVP, connected to the consultancy Bitspire. Maintains bUnit and wrote IfItQuacks, a duck-typing library for C#. Posts often and briefly on new C# and .NET features (C# 14 extensions, .NET 11, EF Core 11), Blazor, and the occasional rant.

author: Adam Sitnik
title: .NET Performance and Reliability
description: Engineer on Microsoft's .NET team (performance and libraries) and maintainer of BenchmarkDotNet. The blog is about profiling and benchmarking .NET; the last post was in January 2023.

author: Kevin Gosse
title: minidump.net
description: Works at JetBrains on ReSharper performance (previously on Datadog's .NET profiler), Microsoft MVP, co-author of Pro .NET Memory Management (2nd edition). Writes deep posts on .NET internals and debugging; the long-running series is "Writing a .NET Garbage Collector in C#".

author: Matt Warren
title: Performance is a Feature!
description: .NET performance specialist and Microsoft MVP who contributed to BenchmarkDotNet and RavenDB. Known for deep dives into the internals of the .NET runtime (CLR/CoreCLR). No posts since 2020.

author: Phil Haack
title: You've Been Haacked
description: Former Microsoft program manager for ASP.NET MVC and NuGet, then worked at GitHub (GitHub Desktop) and founded A Serious Business, maker of the Abbot Slack bot. Joined PostHog in January 2025. Writes about git tools (the author's own tree-me and Spelungit), using PostHog from .NET, and careers.

author: Erik Ejlskov Jensen
title: .NET Data Access and more
description: Principal Specialist at the Danish consultancy delegate and a Microsoft MVP. Author of EF Core Power Tools and the SQLite/SQL Server Compact Toolbox. Recent posts are almost all about SQL Database Projects: SQL Project Power Tools, the T-SQL Analyzer (now in SSMS, Visual Studio and VS Code) and faster .dacpac deployments.

author: Vladimir Khorikov
title: Enterprise Craftsmanship
description: Author of Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns, Pluralsight author and creator of CSharpFunctionalExtensions. Writes about domain-driven design, always-valid domain models and testing. No posts since March 2023.

author: Jon Hilton
title: Practical Engineer
description: UK .NET trainer known for Blazor and ASP.NET Core courses (practicaldotnet.io). The site, now called Practical Engineer ("Engineering for the AI era"), has 2026 posts about working with AI coding tools.

author: Mike Brind
title: Mikesdotnetting (Razor Pages, Blazor)
description: Author of ASP.NET Core Razor Pages in Action; also runs learnrazorpages.com and learnblazor.com. Practical Razor Pages and Blazor tutorials; last post April 2023.

author: Martin Fowler
description: Chief Scientist at Thoughtworks, author of Refactoring, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture and UML Distilled, and a signatory of the Agile Manifesto. The site also publishes long articles by Thoughtworks colleagues. Recent posts: frequent "Fragments" link posts, AI in software development (including write-ups of the 2026 Future of Software Development retreats Thoughtworks held) and a series on giving talks.

author: Simon Willison
description: Co-creator of Django, co-founder of Lanyrd (bought by Eventbrite), and creator of Datasette and the llm command-line tool. Coined the terms "prompt injection" and "lethal trifecta". Posts several times a day about new LLM releases, prompt-injection security and small tools built with AI, and quotes and comments on other people's writing.

author: Peter Steinberger
description: Austrian founder of PSPDFKit (now Nutrient), the PDF SDK company. Came back in 2025 to build with AI agents (VibeTunnel, Poltergeist), then created OpenClaw (originally Clawdbot), the open-source personal agent that went viral in early 2026. Joined OpenAI in February 2026, and OpenClaw moved into an independent foundation. No posts since then.

author: Salvatore Sanfilippo
title: antirez
description: Creator of Redis and, earlier, the network tool hping. Left Redis in 2020 and returned in late 2024, adding vector sets and a new array type. Also built DwarfStar, a local LLM inference engine, largely with coding agents. Writes about programming with AI, Redis design and C, and has written a science-fiction novel (Wohpe).

author: Steve Yegge
description: Worked at Amazon and Google (author of the well-known "Platforms Rant"), then at Grab and Sourcegraph (Cody, Amp). Co-wrote Vibe Coding with Gene Kim. In 2026 released Beads (an issue tracker for AI agents), Gas Town, and Gas Town's rewrite Gas City (tools for running many agents at once). Writes long, opinionated essays about AI and the software industry.

author: Nick Craver
title: Software Imagineering
description: Engineer at Microsoft working on Azure, previously architecture lead at Stack Overflow. Maintains StackExchange.Redis, MiniProfiler, Dapper and Opserver. Best known for the "Stack Overflow: The Architecture" series; no posts since 2020.

author: Jeff Atwood
title: Coding Horror
description: Co-founder of Stack Overflow and Discourse. Rarely writes about programming now. Since 2025 the blog has mostly been about philanthropy, above all the Rural Guaranteed Minimum Income Initiative launched in February 2026.

author: Joel Spolsky
title: Joel on Software
description: Co-founder of Fog Creek (FogBugz, Trello, Glitch) and of Stack Overflow, and author of "The Joel Test" and many classic 2000s essays. Later chaired HASH (a platform for modelling the world) and the Block Protocol. Last post December 2022.

author: Neil Green
title: Neil on Software (Podcast)
description: Articles and an uncensored podcast about the people side of software: dealing with difficult colleagues, the "Dev Types" profiles, hiring, management and crunch. The site has no bio; last post December 2023.

author: Brendan Gregg
title: Systems Performance
description: Leading figure in systems performance: invented flame graphs, created many eBPF and DTrace tools, and wrote Systems Performance and BPF Performance Tools. Worked at Sun, Joyent, Netflix and Intel (as an Intel Fellow), left Intel in December 2025 and joined OpenAI in February 2026. Writes about performance engineering, AI flame graphs and career moves.

author: Kent Beck
title: Software Design: Tidy First?
description: Created Extreme Programming (XP) and test-driven development, co-created JUnit, and signed the Agile Manifesto; has worked at Facebook, Gusto and Mechanical Orchard. Most recent book is Tidy First?. The newsletter covers "augmented coding" with AI "genies", XP as a "long volatility" strategy, and short thinking tools called "Thinkies".

author: Paul Hammant
description: Thoughtworks alumnus who co-created PicoContainer and steered early Selenium (the part that became Selenium RC). Runs trunkbaseddevelopment.com, consults on trunk-based development, and co-wrote Value Stream Mapping for Software Delivery Teams. Recent posts: test selection and red-green-refactor for coding agents, Google-style build systems, and merging.

author: Eduards Sizovs
description: Latvian founder of the DevTernity conference who also trains tech leads (Team Lead Masterclass). DevTernity was cancelled in late 2023 after reports that it had listed fake speaker profiles. Short essays on engineering culture, simplicity and careers; last post March 2023.

author: Bart Wullems
title: The Art of Simplicity
description: Belgian application architect and Microsoft MVP who has posted almost every weekday for years. Short, practical notes on ASP.NET Core, Azure DevOps, authentication (ADFS, Entra ID) and logging, and lately AI coding tools and MCP.

author: Gergely Orosz
title: The Pragmatic Engineer
description: Writes the most popular tech newsletter on Substack. Previously an engineering manager at Uber and an engineer at Skyscanner and Skype/Microsoft. Author of The Software Engineer's Guidebook and host of The Pragmatic Engineer podcast. The blog feed mostly carries the weekly "The Pulse" news roundup: AI at tech companies, layoffs and outages.

author: Vadim Kravcenko
description: Zurich-based CTO who also works as a part-time ("fractional") CTO. Co-founded the agency mindnow, built the SEO tool SEOJuice, and wrote the Python tool pipreqs. Newsletter for developers moving into CTO and tech-lead roles (estimation, tech debt, careers); the latest issue in the feed is from July 2024.

author: Andrew Wulf
title: The Codist
description: Programmer for nearly 40 years who retired in 2021 and now mostly makes digital art. Career retrospectives, programming history and complaints about tools; the last post was in March 2026.

author: Matheus Lima
title: Terrible Software
description: Engineering manager at Tremendous. Short essays on engineering management and on what AI does to trust, speed and thinking at work.

author: Will Larson
title: Irrational Exuberance
description: CTO at Imprint, previously at Carta, Calm, Stripe and Uber. Author of An Elegant Puzzle, Staff Engineer, The Engineering Executive's Primer and Crafting Engineering Strategy, and runs staffeng.com. Writes about engineering leadership and strategy, and lately about using agents in daily work (the "software factory" pattern, code review tooling).

author: Edmond Lau
title: The Effective Engineer
description: Author of The Effective Engineer; was an early engineer at Quip after working at Google, Ooyala and Quora. Now coaches leaders in tech and is building Co·Awaken, a school about relationships. The blog was silent from 2020 until one post in June 2026.

author: Greg Wilson
title: The Third Bit Blog
description: Co-founder of Software Carpentry; editor of Beautiful Code, Making Software and The Architecture of Open Source Applications, and author of Teaching Tech Together and Software Design by Example. Has worked at the University of Toronto, RStudio and Plotly, and posted in September 2026 about looking for work. Writes about teaching programming and research software, and lately Frml, a small language written to learn how program verification works.

author: Damien Bowden
title: Software Engineering
description: Switzerland-based Microsoft MVP specialising in application security and identity: OpenID Connect, OAuth, Entra ID, passkeys and the backend-for-frontend (BFF) pattern. Contributes to angular-auth-oidc-client and runs security workshops. Posts are detailed code walkthroughs, recently BFF with Aspire and SAML with Duende.

author: Shay Rojansky
description: Member of Microsoft's EF Core team and creator and lead of Npgsql, the .NET driver and EF Core provider for PostgreSQL. Writes about database performance and PostgreSQL in .NET; last post May 2023.

author: Barret Blake
title: Barret Codes
description: .NET and Azure developer. The site also has podcasts and a "Silly Little Apps" section. Recent posts: a Multi-Tenant .NET series, self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, FastEndpoints, and who owns the architecture when AI writes the code.

author: Denis Stetskov
title: From the Trenches
description: Kyiv-based tech lead at NineTwoThree who has run engineering teams for more than ten years. Weekly analysis of AI companies, security incidents, policy and geopolitics, focused on the gap between what AI companies claim and what happens in production.

author: Barry Dorrans
title: Ramblings from a .NET Security PM
description: Security technical program manager for .NET at Microsoft and author of Beginning ASP.NET Security. Writes about .NET security and the software supply chain: SSRF, CVEs, SBOMs, package signing and Dependabot.

author: Rick Strahl
description: Founder of West Wind Technologies in Maui and creator of Markdown Monster, West Wind WebSurge and West Wind Web Connection; long-time Microsoft MVP. Long, practical posts drawn from real projects: quirks of hosting ASP.NET Core, Windows desktop apps, WebView2, and JavaScript and CSS basics.

title: samwho
description: Sam Rose, developer educator at ngrok. Known for interactive visual essays (load balancing, hashing, memory allocation, Bloom filters, Turing machines, Big O), each of which takes months; also writes on ngrok's blog (prompt caching, quantization). Only a few posts a year.

author: Sean Goedecke
description: Australian engineer at GitHub. Widely shared posts on how large tech companies actually work, staff-level engineering, and AI; also wrote a book about how the industry changed after 2021. Posts almost every day.

author: Addy Osmani
description: Now a Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic, working on Claude Code. Spent 14 years at Google, first leading developer experience for Chrome (DevTools, Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals), then as a Director in Google Cloud AI. Created Yeoman and TodoMVC and wrote Learning JavaScript Design Patterns, Leading Effective Engineering Teams and Beyond Vibe Coding. Posts are about agentic engineering: "software factories", code quality and agent files.

author: Drew Breunig
description: CEO and co-founder of Cmpnd, which builds on DSPy, and editor of O'Reilly's The Context Engineering Handbook. Previously ran strategy and data science at PlaceIQ and then Precisely, and advises the Overture Maps Foundation. Known for context-engineering posts such as "How Long Contexts Fail"; now writes about agent harnesses, system prompts and "prompt debt".

author: Swizec Teller
description: Slovenian-born engineer based in San Francisco, formerly a tech lead at the health startup Tia. Author of Serverless Handbook, Senior Mindset and Scaling Fast, with a long-running newsletter. Writes about engineering in fast-growing startups, and lately AI in teams: auto-merging PRs, code review load, and code becoming cheap.

author: Uwe Ricken
title: SQL Server Blog
description: Managing director of db Berater GmbH near Darmstadt, a company that works only on SQL Server. Microsoft Certified Master for SQL Server 2008 and Data Platform MVP. Writes in-depth posts on execution plans, statistics, locking, partitioning, and temp tables versus CTEs, and also runs workshops.

title: SQLPerformance.com
description: Group blog started by SQL Sentry (later SentryOne), now owned by SolarWinds. Its regular authors include Paul White, Aaron Bertrand, Erin Stellato, Itzik Ben-Gan, Paul Randal, Glenn Berry and Jonathan Kehayias. Recent posts mix DBA topics (SQL Agent job history, archive tables) with SolarWinds product announcements.

author: Matthias Kainer
description: CTO and co-founder of INXM, with earlier leadership roles at Thoughtworks, Volocopter and Isar Aerospace. Writes about software delivery, explaining LLMs, and leadership.

author: Hillel Wayne
description: Consultant and teacher of formal methods (TLA+, Alloy), author of Practical TLA+ and Logic for Programmers (in print since mid-2026), and writer of the Computer Things newsletter. Known for "The Crossover Project", interviews with people who worked in both traditional engineering and software. Posts rarely, on logic, specifications and programming history.

author: Benjamin Cane
description: Distinguished Engineer at American Express, working on the architecture of its payments platform. Short weekly posts on distributed systems, reliability and architecture: timeouts, retries, queues, latency and gRPC.

author: Gui Ferreira
description: Porto-based Microsoft MVP and educator (Black Lab Studios), with courses on Dometrain about xUnit, TDD, clean code and Claude Code, plus a YouTube channel. Writes about testing (xUnit v3), architecture and rules files for AI tools; last post February 2026.

author: Armin Ronacher
title: Armin Ronacher's Thoughts and Writings
description: Creator of Flask, Jinja, Click and Werkzeug, and of the Rust libraries insta and MiniJinja. Spent about ten years at Sentry, then co-founded Earendil in 2025 (the company Mario Zechner joined). Writes about agentic coding, what AI does to programmers, Rust and open source.

author: Oleksii Nikiforov
title: N+1 Blog
description: Lead Software Engineer at EPAM and an AI coach. Maintains Keycloak.AuthServices, a popular .NET auth library. The blog used to be mostly .NET and Aspire; recent posts are almost all about Claude Code (plugins, Claude Code Hub, "Redline" code review).

author: Mario Zechner
description: Austrian developer, creator of libGDX, the cross-platform game framework, and long involved in the Spine animation tool. Built the minimal "pi" coding agent, and in April 2026 joined Earendil, Armin Ronacher's company, taking pi along. Writes about coding agents and MCP versus command-line tools, and earlier about a grocery-price tracker that Wired covered.

author: Vivek Trivedy
description: Leads Applied Research at LangChain Labs (continual learning, "harness engineering", curating data to improve agents). Previously worked at an agent startup and on health AI at AWS, and did a PhD at Temple. Posts are about agent harnesses and LangChain's Deep Agents.

author: David Crawshaw
description: Co-founder of Tailscale and former member of Google's Go team. In 2026 started another company, exe.dev, which is building a cloud. Older posts cover Go, SQLite and networking; recent ones are about programming with LLMs and agents.

author: Chris Parsons
description: Former CTO who has founded five startups. Now advises CEOs and executive teams on adopting AI, and has shipped AI systems to production (for example an LLM meal generator for Cherrypick). Articles are practical AI-at-work advice, plus a weekly newsletter.

author: Rémi Louf
title: The Typical Set
description: Co-founder and CEO of .txt and creator of Outlines, the structured-generation library for LLMs. Previously maintained Blackjax and Aesara (Bayesian statistics and MCMC sampling). The site is a "digital garden" of notes, revived in 2026.

author: Willem van den Ende
description: Partner at QWAN and an early Dutch Extreme Programming (XP) and test-driven development (TDD) coach. Now writes about agentic engineering, small homemade evals and building with open-weights models. Also wrote the engine the blog runs on, "Firehose".

author: Aaron Brethorst
description: Executive Director of the Open Transit Software Foundation, which runs OneBusAway; previously the volunteer lead for its iPhone app. Lately writes about agentic AI (agent Skills, Claude Code) and engineering management.

author: Wes McKinney
description: Creator of pandas, co-creator of Apache Arrow and author of Python for Data Analysis. Founded Voltron Data and Ursa Labs, and now runs Kenn Software (agent developer tools such as roborev and msgvault) while also working as Principal Architect at Posit. Recent posts are about agentic engineering ("The Mythical Agent-Month").

author: Jason Taylor
description: Microsoft MVP and solutions architect focused on .NET and Azure. Created the Clean Architecture Solution Template. Posts rarely (the last time before March 2026 was in 2022).

author: Brent Ozar
description: SQL Server consultant and trainer, Microsoft Certified Master and founder of Brent Ozar Unlimited. Best known for the free First Responder Kit (sp_Blitz and related scripts). Blogs on performance tuning, Office Hours sessions and SQL Server news.

author: Vincent Driessen
description: Works at Liveblocks; previously CTO of GitPrime. Best known for "A successful Git branching model" (git-flow), rq and pip-tools. Writes about API design, TypeScript and Python. Posts rarely.

author: Bryan Cantrill
title: The Observation Deck
description: Co-founder and CTO of Oxide Computer. Before that, 14 years at Sun (co-creator of DTrace) and 9 at Joyent. Co-hosts the Oxide and Friends podcast and writes about systems, engineering culture and industry history.

author: Dave Rupert
description: Builds web components at Microsoft and co-hosts the ShopTalk podcast. Co-founded the agency Paravel (which made FitVids.js) and the startup Luro. Writes about HTML, CSS, web components and the web in general.

author: Daniel Stenberg
title: curl, open source and networking
description: Founder and lead developer of curl, a full-time job through wolfSSL. Active in the IETF HTTP and QUIC working groups. The blog covers curl releases, security vulnerabilities, open-source maintenance and the flood of AI-generated bug reports.

author: Martin Kleppmann
description: Author of Designing Data-Intensive Applications (the 2nd edition came out in 2026) and Associate Professor at Cambridge. One of the people behind Automerge and local-first software; co-founded Rapportive, which LinkedIn bought. Posts rarely; the subjects are distributed systems, cryptography and formal verification.

author: Joe Heck
title: Rhonabwy
description: Seattle engineer and manager; formerly CTO at SunLink, a director at Dell EMC and VP of Engineering at Nebula. Wrote Kubernetes for Developers and Using Combine, and takes part in Swift's documentation (DocC) working group. Writes about Swift, DocC, and lately agentic coding.

author: Paul Dix
description: Founder and CTO of InfluxData and creator of the InfluxDB time-series database. The site says it covers databases, distributed systems and open source, but so far its only three posts are about AI and programming.

author: Giles Edwards-Alexander
title: overwatering.org
description: CTO for Europe, the Middle East and India at Thoughtworks since 2025. Previously Chief Technology and Product Officer at Kooth, which listed on the stock market in 2020, and founder of Pandita. Writes about engineering, refactoring and conference notes, plus books and restoring land in North Wales.

author: James Randall
description: Veteran developer who started on a BBC Micro, later an architect and CTO, and known in the Azure/.NET world for Function Monkey. Writes about AI-assisted development (Onus) and retro projects such as a 4X game and a BBC Micro emulator.

title: No One's Happy
description: Anonymous writer covering what technology, media and capitalism do to everyday life, explaining how the systems work. Has articles (one, for example, on Claude Max plan limits) and a short-form "log" with its own feed, /log.xml.

title: Agentic Patterns
description: Curated by Nikola Balić (nibzard), who builds AI agents and tools (skillctl, Wire) and wrote The Agentic AI Handbook. The site is an open catalogue of about 200 agent patterns, built from the community awesome-agentic-patterns repository. The feed announces new and updated patterns, often dozens in one day.
